Prince Maidono"...Chief. This is certain? No room for a mistake?"
Chief"...Unfortunately, Highness. Several separate channels have brought me the same information."
Chief"At the Oyumi Kubo's headquarters, preparations for a major military operation have begun."
Prince Maidono"And the target...?"
Chief"Nothing has been announced. But taking the present situation into account... most likely..."
Prince Maidono"Yes. Not much mystery left there."
Chief"...Only their slow preparations are in our favor. They cannot judge our strength, I suspect."
Chief"We still have time to take some action."
Prince Maidono"...Even so, Chief."
Chief"..."
Prince Maidono"My luck, it seems, has finally said bas. Enough."
Chief"No, Highness. Kyoto remains. Even the shogunate cannot send its soldiers into the Imperial Palace."
Chief"I shall arrange your departure from Kamakura immediately—"
Prince Maidono"That will not do, Kikuchi..."
Chief"...Highness."
Prince Maidono"If I withdraw now, there is no coming back. As Prince Maidono, I am finished..."
Prince Maidono"Politically dead, but keeping myself alive? After all this plotting, I should take no responsibility at all? That is a very ugly way to survive."
Chief"But—"
Prince Maidono"I have some shame left. So have you."
Prince Maidono"On that battlefield, remembering it was the one thing that kept us human. Was it not?"
Chief"Highness..."
Ten Champions Member A"An admirable resolve. Then permit me to grant you an honorable death, Your Highness Prince Haruhiro of Maidono."
Chief"What—"
Prince Maidono"Who is there!?"

I lowered my head. Helplessness seemed to be pushing it down.

Nothing I could do?

Part of this was my doing, no doubt about that. A different course from me could have brought a different outcome.

And now I could do nothing? Only save myself and run?

Bring down the Silver Star. Yes. That duty must be fulfilled before anything else.

But... even so. Even then...

en.html:
Her clear voice finally shut down every objection.

No answer came out of me. There were things to say. Surely there were things to say against faith this reckless.

But saying them, I could not manage. She had overwhelmed me. The prince and Chief were probably in much the same condition.

This was not the Ichijou of before. Not even yesterday's girl, shaking at the horror of killing.

Before, she had only the will. Carry justice through. Never forgive those who trampled the weak with violence. The will alone.

A child's weightless dream. No achievement to support it, no means even to make it real.

Now, different.

She had confidence. Certainty that she could destroy evil. The pride of knowing her own blade could condemn the powerful wicked, however arrogant, however far beyond the law.

She had defeated Doushin Yusa. And now, by sheer willpower, she had stepped over her terror of that killing.

The girl had become someone new.
An executor of justice.

What Ichijou Ayane had wanted to become—finally, she had reached it.

These two knowing was hardly a problem, admittedly.

I looked again at Okabe's surviving children. Princess Sakurako seemed unchanged—no. There was a shadow from what she had suffered, and a strength from having come through it. I could glimpse both now.

The other one, Kuronose Douji, was covered in black military clothing. His features were unclear. The princess's younger brother should still be young. From his build, perhaps around twenty.

He was examining us also. Not much approval for the man with the gloomy face, apparently. One inspection, then his eyes left me.

The earnest girl beside me received respect from the beginning. Looking at her small frame, nothing like a warrior's, he seemed to respect her more.

In that little body, such a feat. His sigh and bowed gaze seemed to say it.
Something close to worship was in those eyes.

en.html:
—Something was wrong.
Something did not fit.

No... was the problem with me? They seemed so far away.

One will was gathering everyone in this room. Only I remained awake.

...My wandering eyes found the assassin's corpse. Dead for some time now, beginning to stiffen.
One stroke, cut in two. Not a trace of hesitation in that sword.

Ichijou would not hesitate anymore.
She would keep fighting.

Princess Sakurako, Kuronose Douji, the Chief, the prince... all of them had that same will. Fight, without doubt.

Only I was hesitating?

No. Why should I? With Ichijou's help, the curse need not bind me.

Doushin Yusa had died through my actions, but I had asked nobody for a death in payment. No good person had been killed by me.

The relief of that went deep.

Then... what was the difficulty?

Raichou Imagawa was not an innocent man. During the Osaka massacre, foremost among Rokuhara's crimes, he had reportedly commanded the Umeda district. Burned the entire area with its people inside. Thousands of lives taken.

If Ichijou said he should die, I could only agree. No defense came to mind. No wish to defend him, either.

So where was the problem? What objection remained to fighting alongside her and the prince?

A paradise at the end, I did not expect. But surely the prince could make Yamato easier to live in than Rokuhara did. Easier than under GHQ occupation.

Was that wrong?

The opposite.

Justice was here.
Justice worth believing in.

Then fight for it. Why should that not be enough?

However much I fought, however much evil I killed—
I no longer had to kill the good.

Wrong.
Wrong.
Wrong.

Of all things, why could I not accept that?

I did not understand.

What was catching inside my mind?
Why was my heart hesitating?

What... had I forgotten?
